imha-advocacy.description: Independent Mental Health Advocate for all patients (informal and detained)

steps.title: Confirm Criteria
steps.content: All patients have the right to access an Independent Mental Health Advocate (IMHA), whether informal (voluntary) or detained under the Mental Health Act. Detained patients include those under Section 2, Section 3, Section 4, Section 5(2)/5(4), CTO (Section 17A), Section 37, Section 37/41, or Section 47/49. Informal patients are not detained but still have access to advocacy services.

safeguarding.title: Safeguarding Adults - Making a Referral
safeguarding.description: S.42 Care Act 2014 - when and how to refer

steps.title: Check the Criteria (S.42)
steps.content:
Section 42 of the Care Act 2014 - all three must apply:

1. The adult has care and support needs
2. They are experiencing, or at risk of, abuse or neglect
3. Because of those needs, they cannot protect themselves

No 'significant harm' threshold. If in doubt, refer.
steps.checkboxLabel: I confirm this meets adult safeguarding criteria (S.42)

steps.title: Consent
steps.consentYesDesc: I have discussed the referral with the adult and they consent
steps.consentNoDesc: Consent not given or not sought - proceeding due to risk (record your reasons)
steps.consentYesNote: Consent was obtained from the adult.
steps.consentNoNote: Consent was not obtained; referral made on risk grounds (reasons recorded on the referral).
steps.informedQuestion: Separately - have you told the patient the referral is being made?
steps.content:
Best practice is to get consent before referring. However:

- Don't let consent stop you if you're genuinely worried
- You can override consent if there's immediate risk of harm or risk to your own safety
- If you can't get consent, explain why in the referral
- Always try to inform the person you're making a referral, even if consent wasn't obtained
- Consider whether the person has capacity to consent

Having consent is ideal but not essential. A referral without consent is better than no referral at all.

steps.title: Select Area
steps.content: Which local authority area is the patient from? This determines where to send the safeguarding referral.

steps.title: Writing a good referral
steps.content:
Read the questions on the form carefully and answer every one as fully as you can. These pointers come from the local safeguarding team's own "what a good referral looks like" guidance.

What to cover:
• What have you seen (where, when)? What have you heard (when, who from)?
• Basic information about the adult at risk. What care and support needs do they have? Why are they unable to protect themselves from the abuse or neglect? Do they have capacity to make decisions about keeping themselves safe?
• Basic information about the person alleged to be causing the harm. Do they have care and support needs of their own? Do they work with children or vulnerable adults? Are they in a position of trust? Any history of posing a risk?
• Why are you worried, and what type of abuse or neglect is it - physical, emotional, sexual, neglect, financial, organisational, self-neglect, modern slavery, exploitation or discrimination? Has a crime been committed? Was the harm intended or ill-informed?
• What is the impact on the adult now, and what is it likely to be if agencies do not become involved?
• What have you already tried to reduce the risk? Include outcomes of any referrals to other services, and what protective factors are in place.
• What does the adult want to happen as a result? Enquiries work better when they are person-centred and led by the adult at risk.
• Who is in their professional and informal support network? If they would have substantial difficulty taking part themselves, who could represent them - consider an advocacy referral.

Separate fact from opinion:
You can give a professional opinion, but say clearly that it is one. For example: the adult said "I wanted to give the person money", however in my view they were coerced into that decision because... then list the evidence - use of substances, witnessed control or coercion, impairment of mind or brain.

Pitfalls that weaken a referral:
• Answering "Unknown" or leaving blanks. Say why you do not know.
• Formalising or sanitising the language used. Quote people's actual words, including swearing and slang, and add clarification of what they meant. This can become evidence in court - do not leave room for dispute.
• Too little detail on the concern or its impact. A good referral does not say someone has "a chaotic lifestyle" - it evidences the lived experience. Missed their last four appointments in six months. Homeless - sleeping on the street, or staying with friends, and which friends? Not in work, education or training. Poor home conditions - damp, refuse piling up, flies, animal waste on carpets. One litre of vodka a day, on a methadone programme. Said they would kick their head in if they told anyone.
• Writing it in a way that is not for sharing. Would you be happy for the person you are writing about to read it over your shoulder? Never imply the adult is complicit in or responsible for the abuse. Victim-blaming language normalises and minimises what happened, and gets a weaker response.
• Delay. If you are worried, the referral is a priority.

The top tip:
You are not telling a story, you are sharing concerns about an adult at risk. Keep them at the centre. What is a day in their life like? What are you worried about? What needs to happen for things to get better?

A safeguarding enquiry is not the finish line. Safeguarding stays everybody's responsibility, including for adults who have already been through an enquiry.

wagoll.label: What a 'Good' Safeguarding Referral Looks Like

steps.title: Submit Referral
steps.content: Ring and discuss the case first, then submit the form.

steps.title: Case Note Entry
steps.content: Copy this text to add to the patient's case notes:
steps.clipboardText: Adult Safeguarding concern raised to [DERBY CITY/DERBYSHIRE COUNTY] on [DATE]. Concern relates to suspected [TYPE OF ABUSE]. Referral sent via [METHOD]. Reference number: [IF GIVEN]. [CONSENT] Patient [INFORMED] informed of referral.

steps.title: Follow-up Task
steps.content:
Safeguarding is everybody's responsibility - submitting the referral is not the finish line.

Document the referral in patient notes. Log on Datix if required. The S.42 enquiry may task your team with further actions. If the same concerns keep being raised without resolution, escalate to the Assistant Director of Safeguarding.

39% of Derby City and 54% of Derbyshire County referrals become S.42 enquiries. That means many referrals don't meet the threshold this time - but even those that aren't taken up are still logged. They help services build a picture of the person and spot other risk factors over time, so it is always better to refer than to stay silent.

steps.title: GDPR Reminder
steps.content:
Safeguarding overrides normal confidentiality - ensure senior staff are aware of the referral. Delete any downloaded referral forms containing patient data once submitted.

When you save the patient record on SystmOne after documenting anything safeguarding-related, tick 'Safeguarding relevant' at the bottom of the record so it is flagged correctly.

safeguarding-children.title: Safeguarding Children - Making a Referral
safeguarding-children.description: When you're worried about a child (under 18)

steps.title: When to Refer
steps.content:
You should refer when you have concerns about a child (under 18) who may be at risk of:

- Physical abuse or harm
- Emotional abuse or neglect
- Sexual abuse or exploitation
- Neglect (basic needs not met)
- Domestic abuse in the household
- Online harm, exploitation or grooming
- Honour-based abuse, FGM or forced marriage
- Radicalisation or extremism
- Modern slavery or trafficking

This includes children of your patients where parenting capacity may be affected by mental illness, substance use, or domestic abuse.

Think Family - does your patient have children or regular contact with children? Is their mental health affecting their ability to parent safely? Is there domestic abuse in the home?

If there is immediate risk of harm, call 999 first.
steps.checkboxLabel: I confirm there are child safeguarding concerns that require referral

steps.title: Discuss with Family
steps.consentYesDesc: I have discussed the concern with the family and they are aware of / consent to the referral
steps.consentNoDesc: Not discussed with family - doing so would raise the risk or is not appropriate (record your reasons). The child's safety comes first.
steps.consentYesNote: Concern was discussed with the family and they consent to the referral.
steps.consentNoNote: Family consent was not sought or not given; referring without it as seeking it would increase risk (reasons recorded on the referral).
steps.informedQuestion: Separately - have you told the parent/carer the referral is being made?
steps.content:
Best practice is to discuss concerns with the family and gain consent before referring.

However, do NOT seek consent if:
- Doing so would put the child at greater risk
- Doing so would put you or others at risk
- It would compromise a police investigation
- The alleged perpetrator is a family member and may destroy evidence

If you refer without consent, record your reasons clearly in the referral.

steps.title: Select Area
steps.content:
Which area is the child from? This determines which team to contact.

Derby City: Initial Response Team (Mon-Fri 9am-5pm)
Derbyshire County: Starting Point (Mon-Fri 9am-5pm)

steps.title: Referral Forms & Advice
steps.content:
Not sure if the threshold is met? Use the consultation lines before making a formal referral:

- DHCFT Safeguarding Unit: Hidden in demo mode (Option 1)
- Derbyshire Starting Point Consultation: Hidden in demo mode (Mon-Fri 10am-4pm)
- Derby City Professional Consultation Line: Hidden in demo mode (Mon-Fri 10am-4pm)

Refer to the Threshold Document for guidance on levels of need. Assessment tools (EHA, GCP, DVRIM) are available on the DDSCP Documents Library.

Remember to follow up all telephone referrals within 48 hours using the online referral form. Ensure it is recorded on the clinical system (in Comms & Letters).

wagoll.label: Children's Safeguarding Example
wagoll.note: Note the level of detail required

steps.title: Submit Referral
steps.content:
For urgent referrals, telephone first then follow up in writing within 48 hours. Save a copy of the referral in the child's health record.

Include: child's name, DOB, address, school. Parent/carer details. Nature of concern - be specific. How long concerns have been present. Any assessment tools used. Whether the family were informed. Other agencies involved. Your details and contact number.

steps.title: Case Note Entry
steps.content: Document the safeguarding referral in the patient's notes (the parent is your patient):
steps.clipboardText: Child safeguarding concern referred to [DERBY CITY/DERBYSHIRE COUNTY] on [DATE]. Concern relates to [CHILD NAME/DOB]. Nature of concern: [DETAILS]. Referral made via [PHONE/EMAIL]. Reference: [IF GIVEN]. [CONSENT] Parent [INFORMED] informed.

steps.title: Follow-up Task
steps.content:
Children's Social Care should respond within 24 hours of receiving your referral.

- Chase up any outstanding referrals after three working days
- Document the outcome and update relevant agencies
- Be prepared for Social Care to contact you for more information
- If concerns escalate before you hear back, call again

If you disagree with the decision made by Social Care, use the multi-agency dispute resolution escalation protocol to challenge it. Escalation is your professional responsibility.

Safeguarding children overrides normal patient confidentiality. You do not need the parent's consent to refer if a child may be at risk.

steps.title: GDPR Reminder
steps.content:
Safeguarding children overrides normal confidentiality rules. Ensure senior staff and safeguarding lead are aware.

When you save the patient record on SystmOne after documenting anything safeguarding-related, tick 'Safeguarding relevant' at the bottom of the record so it is flagged correctly.

steps.title: Confirm Criteria
steps.content: Patient is homeless or at risk of homelessness within 56 days. This is a statutory Duty to Refer requirement for NHS bodies.
steps.checkboxLabel: I confirm the patient meets homeless referral criteria

steps.title: Patient Consent
steps.content:
Unlike a safeguarding referral, the Duty to Refer is built around the patient's agreement. The Homelessness Reduction Act 2017 asks for their consent to the referral, and to their details going to the housing authority.

[confirm] What to do when you cannot get consent is still being checked with the Trust. A refusal by someone with capacity is not the same as being unable to consent - where a patient LACKS CAPACITY, a best-interests referral may still be appropriate. Do not treat a 'no' here as the final answer: check with your discharge coordinator or the housing team.

Either way, give them the housing contact details, offer to help them self-refer, and record that the offer was made.
steps.consentYesDesc: The patient agrees to the referral and to their details being shared with housing
steps.consentNoDesc: Declined, or unable to consent - read the [confirm] note above before you decide what to do next
steps.consentYesNote: Referral submitted with the patient's consent to their details being shared with housing.
steps.consentNoNote: Consent to the referral was not obtained at this point. Housing contact details were given and the offer of support recorded.

steps.title: Select Area
steps.content: Which local authority area does the patient need housing support from?

steps.title: The SystmOne questionnaire
steps.content:
The Homelessness Referral on SystmOne is two short sections. Have the answers ready before you open it.

Patient details:
• Date of referral
• Reason for referral. Give details such as the dates of being homeless, where the patient was staying prior to admission, and what steps they have taken to prevent homelessness - contacted council services, engaging with a social worker, and so on.
• Last known address
• NHS number
• Current ward
• What benefits does the patient receive, and the total amount of payments received per month?

Patient circumstance:
• Is the patient homeless?
• Do they have any criminal convictions - arson, GBH, sex offender and so on?
• Is the patient fleeing domestic abuse?
• What current community support does the patient have in place on discharge - social worker, CPN, Enablement? Give contact details where you have them.
• Current diagnosis and medication, and can the patient administer their own medication?

Why the detail matters:
The convictions and domestic abuse questions decide what accommodation the council can safely offer. The benefits figure decides what they can afford. Depot arrangements and self-administration decide whether the placement can support the medication. A blank here means a slower placement, not a kinder one.

social-care.title: Social Care (Derby City)
social-care.description: Care Act assessment, S117 referrals & Enablement – Derby City Council Mental Health Social Care

steps.title: Confirm Criteria
steps.content:
Patient has potential Care Act needs, requires Enablement input, or requires Adult Social Care attendance for S117 meetings.

Before referral, confirm:
• Patient is a Derby City resident (check usual address / funding authority)
• If S117 – confirm who has S117 aftercare responsibility
• What was the patient's address when they were made subject to Section 3?

MHA Office number to check if Derby City are S117 responsible: Hidden in demo mode
steps.checkboxLabel: I confirm the patient is a Derby City resident and meets criteria for this referral

steps.title: S117 Status
steps.content:
Is the patient under Section 3, or have they been on a Section 3 in this or a previous admission?

This determines the referral pathway:
• S117 patients – require both a Care Act/S117 referral AND a S117 aftercare meeting before discharge
• Non-S117 patients – follow the standard Care Act referral process

⚠️ IMPORTANT: don't confuse the two meetings. Every patient should have a discharge planning meeting before they leave, whatever their section. The S117 aftercare meeting is a separate requirement that ONLY applies to patients with S117 entitlement – triggered by a Section 3 in this OR any previous admission. S117 status survives readmission, so a patient readmitted informally or under Section 2 who still holds S117 status DOES need one. A patient with no qualifying section in any admission does not. For S117 patients the two are often held as a single combined meeting.

steps.title: What the form asks for
steps.content:
All answers are based on the patient's position and identified needs on the date of referral, not on how they were on admission.

Before the needs section:
Customer details, GP, next of kin and whether an LPA is in place. Then three that people skip: is the customer aware of the referral, do they have capacity to consent to it, and who else is currently involved (CPN, consultant psychiatrist, ward team). Say what the preferred contact arrangements are - if it is the ward for now, say so.

Reason for referral:
Presenting problems, relevant history, physical illness or disability. A brief overview is acceptable, but it has to explain why they cannot go back to where they came from.

The questions that route the referral:
• Has an OT assessment been completed? Initial screening counts - give the date and what it found.
• Would a period of Enablement (6 weeks) be suitable? If not, say why not. "Needs longer-term support" is a rationale; a blank is not.
• Would they be suitable for Talking Point, or for a Local Area Coordinator? Could a Personal Health Budget be considered?

The eight outcome areas:
Personal care · eating and drinking · maintaining the home environment · making decisions · being part of the community · managing their behaviour · being a parent or carer · any unpaid carer's needs and whether a carer's assessment is needed.

For each one, answer Yes / No / Don't know AND write what the patient actually needs. The pattern that works is: what they are like now, and what they are like when unwell. "Currently no concerns. When unwell, has been known to stop eating and drinking due to paranoid beliefs about contamination" tells social care something. "No" does not.

Risk factors:
A past / present grid across violence, suicide, self-harm, self-neglect, exploitation or abuse, and risk to children, plus whether the patient lives alone. Then details of the risk underneath - the grid alone is not enough.

Attach before you send:
Current CPA care plan, risk assessment and the recent outpatients review letter.

steps.title: Submit Referral
steps.content:
All referrals MUST go through duty. Send referral form + supporting documents (care plan, risk assessment, OT assessments if completed). Nursing assessment required if funding may be needed.

⚠️ Missing information or documents? Referral may be closed if relevant information has not been obtained – the ward will be required to resubmit, which may cause delays.

For S117 meeting requests: Send the meeting request form to the same email (7 days notice required).

Note: If the patient has housing needs (regardless of S117 status), 'Duty to Refer' is the correct process – see the Housing / Duty to Refer workflow.
